what: Plan treats any non-empty current_head as same-branch movement, but git rev-parse HEAD is also non-empty in detached HEAD or after a branch switch
scenario_or_breakage: An external coder can detach HEAD or checkout another branch, commit there, and lint-fix-loop will emit applied; ship-pr may then push or continue from the wrong ref instead of preserving the existing head-changed safety net
suggested_fix: Capture the baseline symbolic ref before dispatch with git symbolic-ref --quiet HEAD, compare it after dispatch, and only accept current_head != baseline_head when the symbolic ref is unchanged; add detached and branch-switched regression cases

what: Proposed committed forbidden-path check uses exact path membership while the existing working-tree enforcement treats forbidden paths as prefixes
scenario_or_breakage: A commit that changes files under a forbidden submodule path such as submod/file can bypass the new commit-content check because only submod is in forbidden_paths_file
suggested_fix: Reuse the same case "$path" in "$forbidden_path"|"$forbidden_path"/* matching semantics for committed diff paths, or extract a shared helper so working-tree and committed checks cannot diverge

what: Plan accepts coder commits even when baseline_clean=false, despite the existing design avoiding helper-owned commits over a dirty baseline
scenario_or_breakage: If the parent had unrelated tracked edits before dispatch, a coder commit can accidentally include and push those edits; the proposed forbidden reset path can also discard pre-existing tracked work via git reset --hard "$baseline_head"
suggested_fix: Only treat coder commits as applied when baseline_clean=true, or add explicit preservation/validation for dirty baselines before accepting or resetting; otherwise fail closed with the existing head-changed-after-dispatch reason
